## 2026-10-05 — 0.9.4.47 non-ASCII path scan failure fix

Detail: `docs/build-history/0.9.4.47.en.md`

### Symptom

Clicking Search/Update in the GUI raised a `Search error` dialog.
`%TEMP%\msf_scan.log` recorded `start folder=G:\Downloads\ss_twit` followed one
second later by `failed No mapping ...`. The same folder scanned fine on
September 25-26 and has failed on every attempt since September 28.

The dialog body is `e.what()` caught by `ScanWorker::run()`'s `catch`. On the CLI
the same exception goes uncaught -> terminate -> abort -> 0xC0000409, so it dies
as a silent crash. **Two faces of the same exception.**

### Cause confirmation (verified, not guessed)

The message string was searched across the Qt6 DLLs, the MSVC headers, and 6,240
System32/SysWOW64 DLLs, and it exists **in none of those binaries**. Direct probes
confirmed:

- `fs::u8path(valid UTF-8)` -> ok
- `fs::u8path(CP949 bytes)` -> THROW (exactly this message)
- `fs::path(UTF-8 Korean narrow)` -> THREW (same message)

`fs::u8path()` and the narrow `fs::path(string)` constructor interpret input as
the **ANSI code page (949)**, not UTF-8.

### Cause

`fs::path(file)` and `fs::path(root)` in `canonicalRelativePath()`
(`dataset_fingerprint.cpp:118`) reinterpreted UTF-8 as ACP. It came in with the
dataset fingerprint for the S6 measurement gate (D8a/D8b) and runs at every scan
start, so scans failed "in one second with no file processed". The timeline
matches.

> **Reusable rule**: narrow `fs::path(string)` construction is a forbidden pattern
> in the product. UTF-8 strings must go through `path_from_utf8()`.

### Candidates ruled out by verification

Qt6 `toStdString`/`fromStdString` are UTF-8 based (header + probe confirmed).
`toLocal8Bit()` silently substitutes `?` and never throws.
`Scanner().count/scan`, `MediaPipeline.image/imageBatch`, `db_.upsert`,
`compareFingerprint`, the GPU getters, `detectCpuModel`, and `ProfileStore` were
each verified working by stepwise probes. The index databases were audited
read-only for corrupt paths; none found.

### Fix

One line: `fs::relative(path_from_utf8(file), path_from_utf8(root), ec)`.
The whole product was audited for the same pattern. The `".."`/`"."` ASCII
literals and the `wstring` wide construction in `monitor.cpp` are safe. No other
dangerous site.

### Regression

The existing `unicode_path_test` covered decode, scanner, and DB but not the
dataset fingerprint path, which is how this bug passed. A sixth check was added
in the same file and fixture style.

### Measured

```
CPU Release CTest  103/103 PASS   warning 0 / error 0
GPU Release CTest  104/104 PASS   warning 0 / C4819 0
unicode_path=ok (CPU and GPU)
one non-ASCII file  exit=0 analyzed=1  (was exit=-1073740791)
Korean/Japanese/accented/ASCII mix  scanned=4 analyzed=4 candidates=6 groups=6
```

### Versions

`0.9.4.46` -> `0.9.4.47`. Engine/DB/schema/cache all unchanged.

## 2026-10-05 — 0.9.4.48 GUI Stop unresponsiveness fix

Detail: `docs/build-history/0.9.4.48.en.md`

### Symptom and verdict

After starting a search in the GUI, pressing Stop showed only a "stopping"
message while the actual search continued 10+ minutes with sustained disk reads.

Pressing Stop and the search actually stopping are different things. The message
marks only the start of the request.

### Cause: the fingerprint phase never saw cancellation

The Stop button -> `cancelScan()` -> `worker_->cancel()` ->
`control_.cancel=true` chain was correct. The break was at the start of
`MediaSearchEngine::scan()`:

```cpp
telemetry_.setDatasetFingerprint(msf::computeDatasetFingerprint(root));
```

That function reads every file from first byte to last to build a SHA-256
manifest. It had no cancellation parameter, so it never saw Stop.

Every phase's Stop coverage was verified in code. This was the only gap.
`Scanner::count`, the walker, the consume loop, batches, video ranges, and the
final analyze either check or are bounded, and the inside of `imageBatch` plus a
single FFmpeg decode are bounded by one file.

### Fix

`computeDatasetFingerprint(root, cancel=nullptr)` plumbs the path, checked per
file and during large reads (every 64 KiB chunk). On cancel it returns
immediately with `state="cancelled"` and no partial fingerprint. `"cancelled"`
is telemetry-only with no branching consumer, so it is safe. The default
argument keeps all ~20 existing callers compiling unchanged.

scan() passes `control ? &control->cancel : nullptr`.

### Regression test

`scan_cancel_test` (6 tiny files) verifies flag-set -> incomplete -> resume but
never passes through the fingerprint phase, so it could not catch this bug. The
new `cancel_fingerprint_test` (11 checks) verifies on the production path:

- with cancel pre-set the fingerprint returns `state="cancelled"`, no hash,
  zero files, immediately
- without cancel the same 20 files measure normally
- a pre-cancelled scan reports `completed=false` with zero analysis
- after a cancel the DB reopens and a normal scan completes

No timing assertions. The verdict is the state, so it is deterministic.

### Measured

```
CPU Release CTest  104/104 PASS   warning 0 / error 0
GPU Release CTest  105/105 PASS   warning 0 / C4819 0
```

### GUI reproduction limit

This session is non-interactive, so the actual GUI button click and screen
verification were not performed. Engine-level delivery (tested) and the
button-to-flag wiring (verified by code reading) are confirmed. The GUI click
itself stays **NOT_VALIDATED** and needs user-side verification.

### Not done

Detailed Logs, `color_thumb`, XMP, S5, scheduler/pipeline/GPU redesign, the
benchmark framework — all out of scope.

### Versions

`0.9.4.47` -> `0.9.4.48`. Engine/DB/schema/cache all unchanged.

## 2026-10-05 — 0.9.4.49 Detailed Logs user summary added

Detail: `docs/build-history/0.9.4.49.en.md`

### Requirement and design gap

Detailed Logs carried plenty of internals but no user-facing summary, and the
**duplicate-file total existed nowhere** — a design gap that real GUI log
verification should catch.

Required at-a-glance summary: Duration (`12m 34.5s` shape), per-kind
scanned/analyzed/throughput, duplicate groups/files/pairs split, total row,
time split Total/Image/Video/Matching.

### Fixed meanings

- `SearchReport.groups` counted matched **pairs**, not clusters.
- telemetry `matches.groups` counted distinct union-find roots (**clusters**).
- duplicate pairs = verified matches at or above threshold, per kind
- duplicate groups = distinct clusters, per kind
- duplicate files = files participating in any pair (members), per kind
- A cluster never spans kinds (indexes are separate). Per-kind groups partition
  the total exactly.

### Implementation

Ten `SearchReport` fields plus telemetry `matches`/`images`/`videos` extension
plus the summary block first in the GUI dialog. Throughput is measured analyzed
count divided by measured stage ms (both inputs measured, so legitimate).
Existing detail rows and existing `matches` fields are untouched, so existing
consumers and journal parsing keep working. Nine translation keys added and
registered in the tr-keys gate (`tr_keys=ok checked=56`).

### Regression

New `summary_breakdown_test` 21 checks. Two identical BMPs plus one distinct
file pin `imgPairs=1/imgGroups=1/imgDupFiles=2`, proving files != groups, plus
the partition identities and telemetry JSON agreement. No video path, so every
`vid*` is pinned to 0.

### Measured

```
CPU Release CTest  105/105 PASS   warning 0 / error 0
GPU Release CTest  106/106 PASS   warning 0 / C4819 0
```

### GUI screen

**NOT_VALIDATED.** Non-interactive session, so the actual dialog screen cannot
be checked. The parsing path is unchanged and the new keys are gate-verified.
User-side confirmation needed.

### Versions

`0.9.4.48` -> `0.9.4.49`. Engine/DB/schema/cache all unchanged.

## 2026-10-06 — S4 telemetry reinforcement validity and ranking report (remaining items)

Ranks 1-2 (finishedAt, cancellation phase, fingerprint instrumentation,
totalScannedBytes, series timestamps) are approved to start. This records the
validity investigation and work ranking for the rest (rank 3, GUI, excluded
items). **These are not implemented here.**

### A. Process I/O rate — valid, head of rank 3

**Validity evidence.** The gap between the requirement (measured average IO
read speed) and the current state was confirmed by measurement. `sampleOnce()`
reads both the PDH LogicalDisk rate (`ioReadBps`) and the `GetProcessIoCounters`
cumulatives (`procIoReadBytes`). But in the attached log `diskAvailable=false`
with `samples=1`, so every rate is 0. Cumulatives exist; rates do not.

**Design constraints (document before code).**
- PDH (whole volume) and procIo (process-attributed) are different quantities;
  never overwrite one field with the other. Keep them separate.
- Rates come only from per-sample deltas over the real interval. Deriving
  `bytes÷wall` is forbidden.
- State an explicit minimum-sample rule. With one or fewer samples, do not
  compute an average; keep `not_measured`. Distinguish a measured true zero
  from unmeasured.
- ProcIo cumulatives must be added to the 7-field `series` so per-sample
  deltas are recoverable.

**Ranking reason.** The rule document must precede counting, or the old
zero-masquerading bug recurs. Goes after ranks 1-2.

### B. DB upsert/remove counters — conditionally valid, rank 3

**Validity evidence.** All call sites concentrate in `media_search_engine.cpp`
(6 upsert, 3 remove), and the single-DB-connection comment establishes one
thread, so plain counters suffice with no atomics.

**Design constraints (definition document first).** Four rollback sites exist
(L488,700,707,716). Counting at `upsert()` success over-counts persisted rows
after a later rollback. Therefore define it as **attempt count**, not applied
count, and document it. Attempt count is actually the right meaning for
cancel evidence (how far did it get).

**Ranking reason.** One definition line precedes code. Same phase as A.

### C. GUI display — valid, last

**Validity evidence.** Rendering needs the seven data items first. Translation
keys plus gate registration are mandatory, with JSON-to-display agreement
verified in the `scan_detailed_log_acceptance_test` pattern. Unmeasured values
render as `N/A`, never as 0.

**Ranking reason.** Without data it would be a dialog of empty cells. After A
and B.

### D. Excluded items with reasons

**D-1. Media-type match sextet — excluded (done).** 0.9.4.49 already ships
`imagePairs/Groups/DuplicateFiles` plus the video three, verified
(`summary_breakdown_test` 21 checks). Rebuilding would duplicate. Verification
only.

**D-2. §9 MediaKind rework — excluded (done).** 0.9.4.49 already uses measured
`files_[].kind`, confirmed by code reading not to be extension guessing.
Nothing to touch.

**D-3. Timezone "fix" — excluded (forbidden).** The `localTimeStr()` local-time
without zone is a pre-existing wart, but `finishedAt`/series timestamps must
follow the same convention to stay consistent with existing logs. Changing to
UTC is a separate task; doing it here creates inconsistency.

### E. Final work order (including approved ranks 1-2)

```
Phase A (approved): finishedAt -> cancellation phase -> fingerprint instrumentation
                    -> totalScannedBytes -> series timestamps
Phase B (this report, after A): process I/O rate rule document -> implement,
                    DB counter definition document -> implement
Phase C (last):     GUI summary block + tr keys + gate
Excluded:           media-type sextet, MediaKind rework, timezone fix
```

Phase A alone completes recurrence diagnosis for Stop-class incidents ("when
did it end, where did it stop, who read how much"). Phase B is measurement
quality and can wait.

### Re-measurement caution: an incremental build is not evidence

The first reproduction build was run against an already-built `build-windows-gpu`
tree. It reported 0 C4819, but **nvcc had not been invoked at all** (0
invocations) because the CUDA object was up to date. Reporting that as PASS would
have been unfounded.

To get real evidence only the **mtime** of `src/cuda_backend.cu` was changed, which
forced a genuine recompile. Its content was untouched (`hash-object` identical to
HEAD), and no delete command was used. Only then did the real nvcc command line
appear and C4819=0 become an actual measurement.

> **Reusable rule:** for a "this warning is gone" claim, confirm the compiler
> actually ran. A clean incremental log proves nothing. Check for the compiler
> invocation itself, or force a rebuild, before recording a zero-warning result.

### Document review found: progress had never recorded `619f74a`

Reviewing `development-progress.{ko,en}.md` while writing this report turned up two
defects worth recording separately, because both are the kind that mislead the next
session.

**1. The "Current Status" header contradicted the rest of the same file.** It still
read `0.9.4.44 (6ada90f)` / `0.9.4.44`, while the bottom of the same document
already documented `0.9.4.45` work. Since `AGENTS.md` clause 7 names this document
as the authority for the current state, the authority itself was two versions
stale. Fixed: reference code `0.9.4.45 (619f74a)`, current version `0.9.4.45`.

**2. Neither `619f74a` fix was recorded in progress at all.** Counts for `C4819`,
`-Xcompiler`, `attachParentConsole`, `streamIsRedirected`, and `619f74a` were all
**0** in both language files, while `build-history/0.9.4.45.*` and this work log
documented both changes fully. That is a layer mismatch: detailed history present,
current-state summary absent. A new progress entry now records both fixes with their
verified measurements.

Also corrected: the XMP review entry cited only `97db24f`, its own baseline, without
naming the commit that landed it (`392a4c2`), and `docs/llms.txt` still described
`0.9.4.44 / 6ada90f` as the current regression baseline.

> **Reusable rule:** when work lands, update the *current-state* layer in the same
> change, not only the history layer. A history entry without a progress update
> reads, to the next session, as work that never happened.

The technical content of the XMP and `color_thumb` entries was checked against this
session's measurements and found accurate (38 checks, CPU 102/102, GPU 103/103,
R1-R6 classification, boundary block). The defect was confined to version-baseline
bookkeeping.

## 2026-10-06 — 0.9.4.59 post-build review: phase-1 semantics and phase-2 GUI regression separated
Reference: `0.9.4.59` / `18f101f` · CPU CTest 107/107 · GPU CTest 108/108

### Confirmed semantic bug in phase 1

A **video sampling-generation scope error** is confirmed.

Current `processOne()` inserts both of the following into the general `seen` set:

- videos when `scanVideos=false` (explicitly out of the requested scan scope)
- ignored files (intentionally not analyzed in the current scan)

But 0.9.4.59 uses that general `seen` set for the cancelled-scan `allOldVideosSeen` condition, and its successful-scan branch can call `setSamplingGeneration()` from `r.completed` without checking video scope. Therefore **an image-only scan can advance video sampling generation**. This is a semantic bug caused by treating `seen = discovered/present` as equivalent to `admitted/in-scope processed`.

Required invariant:

- `scanVideos=false` must never mutate `sampling_generation`.
- The generation stamp may advance only after the in-scope video admission/processing boundary is satisfied.
- Keep the general `seen` meaning for deletion detection; introduce a separate video-scope admission state.

### Diagnostic semantic hardening

`finishScan(false)` infers the terminal reason from the live `control->cancel` flag. If a DB error sets `failed=true` and a Stop arrives immediately afterward, the transaction still fails/rolls back but telemetry can be mislabeled Cancelled. Pass an explicit terminal state (`Completed / Cancelled / Failed`) so **a late Stop can never relabel a real failure**.

### Verification additions

1. Complete/cancel an image-only (`scanVideos=false`) scan against a stale generation and prove the video generation stamp is unchanged.
2. Inject a deterministic DB error and prove rollback + `failed=true` telemetry; then prove a late Stop cannot change it to Cancelled.
3. Do not ignore the return value of `setSamplingGeneration()`; verify and document the conservative failure behavior.

### Performance observations from the real GUI run

In the real 0.9.4.59 GUI run with 32,494 images, all images used the GPU image path but reported GPU duty was only **about 0.2%**. The image stage was 567.7 s; verify decode was 25.43 s and WIC copy about 25.07 s, while GPU H2D/kernel/D2H combined was only about 0.31 s. This is not evidence of a broken GPU backend; it points more strongly to **pipeline overlap/starvation between CPU/WIC decode, crop, I/O, and short GPU hashing bursts**.

Even under Maximum (90%), CPU usage oscillated around 20–70% for long intervals and averaged 30.8%. Observed drive I/O also varied around 15–40%. These are classified as **post-1.0 scheduler/pipeline work**, not correctness defects.

### Explicit post-1.0 improvement targets

The image-search engine is **first-pass complete as a product path**. After 1.0, treat the following as a separate performance track:

- refine the real effect of CPU worker occupancy versus the CPU policy
- tune read/decode concurrency and I/O backpressure
- improve decode/crop/hash pipeline overlap and GPU batch persistence
- reduce GPU queue starvation and improve host<->device overlap
- distinguish stage bottlenecks, self-attributed usage, and I/O wait in scheduler decisions
- treat Balanced's initial under-utilization and Maximum's long-period oscillation as a worker-admission/backpressure problem rather than just adding workers

GPU utilization itself is not the objective; end-to-end throughput and system stability are. These tasks stay out of the 0.9.4.59 correctness repair.

### Phase 2 GUI regression

The real GUI reproduced a similar-group list regression: when moving downward with mouse dragging, the vertical scrollbar, or keyboard navigation such as End, the list becomes slow after some distance and eventually returns to the top.

Historical `0.9.3.10` fixed an earlier version of this problem by replacing a simple pixel-offset restore with a **semantic top-item scroll anchor + `PositionAtTop`**. The current 0.9.4 code still contains anchor restoration, but after scans the GUI intentionally keeps `uiTimer_` alive, and `thumbStarved_` can repeatedly trigger `refreshStreaming()` -> `refreshGroupList()` -> `fillPair()` full widget rebuilds. That destructive catch-up path is the leading root-cause candidate for the recurrence.

Phase 2 should compare commit `4c059177efca54463dec62bc0da79cd66fe6507e` with the current `uiTimer_`/`thumbStarved_`/`fillPair()` flow, then avoid destructive full rebuilds during active scrolling or update visible item thumbnails in place. Mouse drag, scrollbar drag, End/PageDown/Home acceptance should be explicit regression checks.

## 2026-10-06 — 0.9.4.60 verification and phase-2 GUI scroll source review

### 0.9.4.60 result

At `6f60b8e`, CPU 108/108 and GPU 109/109 passed, including 35 checks in `scan_generation_scope_test`. Existing video-cancel 26 and image-drain 7 checks remain green. Source review matches the reported generation/terminal-state implementation.

### Important GUI regression correction

The `0.9.3.10` semantic anchor based on `itemAt(QPoint(2,2))` is still present. Therefore the statement that the historical fix disappeared is incorrect.

The stronger issue is architectural: the current 0.9.4 code keeps the UI timer alive after scans and `refreshStreaming()` treats `thumbStarved_` alone as permission to perform a full rebuild. The fresh-thumbnail budget is only four per tick, so this condition can persist for a large group list.

That means `fillPair()` may `clear()` and recreate the entire middle tree/grid while the user is actively scrolling. The anchor can restore the viewport after the destructive rebuild, but it does not make scrollbar drag state, keyboard navigation, or in-flight layout/paint safe against widget destruction.

Therefore the first phase-2 target is **eliminate/defer unnecessary full rebuilds**, not rewrite the anchor again.

### Recommended correction structure

- Full `rebuildGroups() + fillPair()` only when group membership/order/search actually changes.
- Thumbnail-only catch-up updates existing visible items in place instead of recreating the list.
- Add a scrollbar-interaction and recent wheel/key-scroll cooldown so destructive rebuilds are mutually exclusive with user navigation.
- Keep the 0.9.3.10 anchor as a safety net for cases that genuinely require a full rebuild.

The exact Qt internal step that finally clamps the scroll position to zero has not yet been proven by runtime instrumentation. Do not guess and insert a Qt-specific workaround.

### Regression acceptance candidates

- tree view: End -> timer tick -> preserve top item/scroll value
- tree view: vertical scrollbar drag across a timer tick -> drag remains continuous and position is preserved
- grid view: End/PageDown/Home + timer tick -> anchor preserved
- continuous mouse-wheel scrolling while a timer tick occurs -> no full rebuild
- thumbnail catch-up immediately after scan must not trigger excessive detail/right-pane refresh while the user scrolls.

## 2026-10-08 - 0.9.4.74 merged audit / telemetry-exit crash / progress and resume. Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.74.en.md
### Audit comparison and diagnosis
Compared the ChatGPT backpressure/auto-resume, Claude per-file quickHash/batch-count, Kimi saved-config, and Grok signal-order findings against C++ source, user logs, and dumps. The captured .72 log records `backend process exited (code -1073740791)`; no watchdog timeout. The dump reports 0xC0000409, parameter 0x7 (FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT), fault RIP ucrtbase+0xA527E. `MSF_TEST_THROW_WALKER` injected an exception during an active telemetry sampler. The same seam passes after the fix.
Supervisor restart is scheduled before failure UI. MainWindow stores `BackendScanConfig`, reports the first restart non-modally, and resumes once on READY. backend_e2e_test proves forced kill -> READY -> automatic START_SCAN -> FINISHED.

`Scanner::count()` prepass now reports every 2,000 directory entries and logs `scanPhase=count begin/done`. Heartbeat counters reset per scan. The existing consumer `walked` contract remains unchanged; new producer `readProgress` reports in-scope, non-ignored files after quick-hash and bounded queue admission. `scan_stream()` reports completed hash batches. Tests assert target count, producer read count, and listing progress.

## 2026-10-10 - 0.9.4.82 EXIF-rotated image WIC FlipRotator runaway removed. Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.82.en.md
### Diagnosis (probe-measured)
Built a probe from the 0.9.4.79 large-scan report (177,120 images, total 177 min, image stage 117 min, slowest files 343-480 s each) and reproduced it. The five slow files are all EXIF orientation=6 + 12 MP (4000x3000/4032x3024). File and disk are healthy (raw read ~10 ms, GDI+ decode 30-60 ms). In the product WIC path, `IWICBitmapFlipRotator` (between decoder and scaler) plus Fant makes `CopyPixels` take **151 s** for one orientation=6 12 MP image (22 ms unrotated). The product decodes each image 3 times -> about 450 s per file, matching the report. A random 500-file sample had 0 rotated images, so the pathological set is very small (estimated ~9 files, about 38% of the wall time).
### Implementation
Added `applyOrientationPixels` (software rotate/flip, channels 1/4) to `image_decoder.cpp` and moved orientation to after scaling. `decodeWicBranches` keeps `src=frame` and, for 90/270, swaps the oriented w/h and computes the pre-rotation scale target `(h,w)`; `decodeWicFileAspectColor` likewise. WIC's composition order (FlipHorizontal first, then rotation) was pinned by measuring a synthetic pattern.
### Verification
CPU CTest 122/122, GPU CTest 123/123. `xmp_orientation_test` 38 checks, `shared_wic_source_probe --selfcheck` PASS, other related tests PASS. `applyOrientationPixels` vs WIC `FlipRotator` 98/98 byte-identical (7 transforms x 7 sizes x gray/BGRA). After the fix, about 70-80 ms per file (about 6000x).
### Performance / tuning experiment index
P-0.9.4.82-fliprotator-runaway / P-0.9.4.82-orient-after-scale — PASS (performance). Hypothesis: slow files are a WIC rotation (FlipRotator) runaway. Baseline 0.9.4.81. Dataset: top five files from `G:\Downloads\ss_twit` (orientation=6, 12 MP). Raw: rotator->scaler 150,916/151,563/156,374 ms, scaler only 22 ms, scaler->rotator 654-765 ms. software vs old 88/1024 +/-1, software vs WIC reorder 0/1024. Limitation: rotated-image fingerprint up to +/-1 LSB. Revisit: WIC/Windows updates; GPU/NVDEC decoder paths.
### Why option 1 was chosen
Chose option 1 (scale-first + software rotate). Reasons: (1) 22 ms/call, faster than WIC reorder (B, 654-765 ms) and the old path (151 s). (2) software rotate is 0/1024 byte-identical to "apply WICBitmapFlipRotator to the scaled source" (same result as WIC-native rotation), and probe7 showed 98/98 match vs WIC. (3) removing the FlipRotator eliminates the whole class of decoder-side rotation interactions. (4) it is a small-buffer pixel permutation directly verified by xmp_orientation_test/probe7. (5) one helper covers all four decode paths. (6) the cost is +/-1 LSB -> engine patch bump.
### Unselected alternatives (recorded, detailed algorithms in build-history/0.9.4.82.en.md §7)
A. Byte-identical materialization (rotate full-res into an IWICBitmap then scale; order preserved): probe incomplete at `hr=0x80070216`, full-res bitmap cost (12 MP ~ 36-48 MB per call), byte-identity unverified -> retry first if the engine bump is unacceptable. B. WIC reorder (scaler->rotator, WIC-only): 654-765 ms, byte-identical to software -> if manual pixel code is disallowed. C. Decoder-native `IWICBitmapSourceTransform` (DCT scale + rotate in one pass): not measured, per-codec support/bytes parity uncertain -> when confirmed. D. Metadata cache option (OnDemand -> OnLoad): not measured, unrelated to rotation -> if metadata cost reappears.
### Version
0.9.4.81 -> 0.9.4.82. `kEngineVersion 1.5.0 -> 1.5.1` (rotated-image verdicts revalidate). DB/schema/cache unchanged.

### Implementation
Reordered `ScanWorker::run()` from count -> revalidate -> quick-load -> walk to **revalidate -> quick-load -> count -> walk**. quick-load now precedes count, so stored groups (+ thumbnails from the ThumbnailStore disk cache) reach the GUI right after scan start. revalidate stays before quick-load so false positives never remain on screen (it persists survivors only).

Pre-sending allPaths_ via a `results` preliminary flag -> rejected: `refreshFileViews` renders only the selected group and allPaths_ is not consumed for display; showing stored matches before revalidate leaves false positives. Chose the reorder only (no IPC change).

## 2026-10-15 - 0.9.4.104 Batched recycle + batched cache drop + phase timing. Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.104.en.md
### Problem
User reports: (1) recycle + list refresh of multi-checked files too slow. (2) Many previews missing from the GUI after delete/move (not actually deleted). Survivors mostly reference files.
### Cause
(1a) `deleteSelected` one `SHFileOperationW` per file = N shell round-trips (GUI thread). (1b) `moveSelected` per-file rename/copy (GUI thread). (1c) `prunePaths` full `dropThumbCache` scan per deleted file (O(3000xN), GUI thread). (2) Full middle-pane rebuild re-requests unaffected groups + pending-cap-2000 tracking erasure drops arrivals as unknown (permanent blanks) + no backend dedupe. "Only references remain" is cache-hit bias.
### Implementation
`recycleFiles()` single shell call (per-file existence verify + retry, partial semantics kept). `dropThumbCache(QSet)` single sweep (single-path overload removed). `delete`/`move`/`prune` wall-time logs. Move loop, full rebuild, backend untouched (next-build C/D/E).
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123. GUI --version 0.9.4.104. Existing suite (no new shell-dependent registrations). Field feel + logs pending.
### Performance experiment index
P-0.9.4.104-recycle-batch / P-0.9.4.104-dropbatch — status PASS (implementation). Wall-time measured values: Not measured (awaiting user-log `delete`/`prune` lines). Complexity analysis: shell round-trips N->1, cache drop 3000xN->3000 (not measurements, evident from structure). Limits: move loop, full rebuild, backend storm unresolved. Revisit: `IFileOperation`+progress if logs show `recycleMs` dominating, incremental update (D) if `rebuildMs` dominates.
### Version
0.9.4.103 -> 0.9.4.104. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-15 - 0.9.4.105 Thumbnail-storm root fix + detail ping-pong fix + immediate index reflection + background file I/O. Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.105.en.md
### Problem
User report: preview loss after delete/move persists after 0.9.4.104 ("loading time slightly reduced, same problem") -> fix the root cause and finish all deferred items (D/E/F/C/detail-text).
### Cause
(D) Every row of a full rebuild fired a `fileThumb` request (thousands); the pending-cap 2000 `erase(begin())` dropped in-flight tracking so late answers were discarded as unknown (permanent blanks). (Detail) `requestFileMeta` deduped in-flight only -> a duration-less image answer made `refreshDetail` ask again -> rebuild -> ask again: an endless ping-pong (form rows deleted/recreated repeatedly, text appeared and vanished). (F) delete/move never updated the stored index. (C) File operations ran synchronously on the GUI thread.
### Implementation
(D) `thumbBulkFill_` (no requests during bulk fills) + visible-only pump on fill completion + refuse-at-cap + tracking-map clear on backend loss. (Detail) `fileMetaAsked_`/`fileMetaRequestCount_` + `refreshDetail` only on displayed change. (E) `ThumbnailStore::kMemMax` 256->1024. (F) `Database::forget` (files+matches+thumbs, one transaction) + `FORGET_PATHS` IPC + `BackendSession::forgetPaths` (refused during scans) + supervisor/loopback wiring + delete/move/rename/cut-paste calls (ignore list excluded). (C) Recycle/move on worker threads (`QThread::create`; recycle uses `CoInitializeEx` APARTMENTTHREADED) + `newFileOpDialog` progress (move cancel supported); prune/forget/log run back on the GUI thread.
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123. GUI --version 0.9.4.105. Scroll regression phase 17 `pending=2 items=120` (no per-row storm) + phase 18 `m1=240 m2=240` (ping-pong stopped) + `database_test forget=ok`. Field checks pending: bulk operation feel, dialog visuals, real-process `forget` log.
### Performance experiment index
P-0.9.4.105-bulkfill / P-0.9.4.105-fileop-bg — status PASS (implementation). Measured: request count in the scroll test (all rows 120 -> visible 2, CPU offscreen); wall times otherwise Not measured (awaiting field logs). Limits: immediate indexing of a moved file's new location is out of scope (next scan); FORGET_PATHS refused during scans. Revisit: per-row incremental update if `rebuildMs` persists; `IFileOperation`+progress if `recycleMs` persists.
### Version
0.9.4.104 -> 0.9.4.105. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

### Problem

Audit: 100.0% appears only at hash distance 0 (blend max 99.2) and the fast path (>=97) skips SSIM there. Probe: all three pairs distance 0; forced SSIM 99.34/99.82/99.69%.

User index (177,594 files / 15,187 pairs): of 11,817 displayed-100.0% pairs, 3,511 content-identical and 8,306 derivatives (11,995 files). Transport: LiveMatch -> BackendMatch -> IPC `identical` -> matchRows 4th field (3-field rows still accepted). GUI `contentFlag_` (bit1/bit2) + `pctText` badge ("identical content"/"perceptual match"). Reference-file convention unchanged. tr-keys 69 -> 71.
### Verification

### Performance experiment index

Candidate P-0.9.4.106-a-blend — status NOT ACCEPTED (cost): 8,306 pairs / 11,995 files, G: decode median 43.0 ms / mean 65.9 ms vs C: 4.1 ms (probe, 80 samples), serial +8.0-12.3 min. - .106 acceptance remains unverified: visually check the badge for three derivative pairs and byte-identical copies. UI phase 19 checks part of the flag, but the actual Backend-process IPC `identical` field reaching the GUI badge needs a dedicated real-process assertion or field evidence.

Separate the historical `cudaAvailable=False` run from its build/runtime conditions; define matched conditions and repetition count before another G: DBV measurement.

### Independent gates requiring OpenCode review

#### G4 — IPC backpressure / slow consumer

In current `src/backend_main.cpp`, `BackendServer::send()` writes to stdout and calls `flush()` synchronously, while `onMatchesBatch()` chunks MATCHES into batches of 500. This proves chunking, not by itself the bounded asynchronous outgoing queue and non-blocking scan behavior required by the implementation brief. No slow-GUI-consumer stress test was identified in the current E2E inventory.

OpenCode checklist:
1. Trace the actual blocking path from write/flush through the event loop and scan worker, and inspect bounds on pending storage such as `ScanWorker::pending_` across the current HEAD.
2. Add or run a reproducible stress test that delays/pauses GUI stdout consumption. Check bounded memory/queued data, losslessness of MATCHES_BATCH/FINISHED/FAILED, and the required coalescing of progress/health messages.
3. Do not mark G4 PASS before evidence exists. Propose a minimal fix only if a real contract violation is demonstrated.

#### G6 — Windows Job Object termination guarantee

Current `gui/backend_supervisor.cpp` includes `CreateJobObjectW`, `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, and `AssignProcessToJobObject`. In the reviewed code, the return values from `SetInformationJobObject` and `AssignProcessToJobObject` do not appear to be checked/logged. Current `backend_e2e_test.cpp` tests forced Backend termination and restart, but does not explicitly prove that Backend exits when the GUI parent process itself is terminated.

OpenCode checklist:
1. Review results and `GetLastError()` handling/logging for job creation/configuration, `OpenProcess`, and `AssignProcessToJobObject`; decide how to detect a state where protection was not established.
2. Review/add a Windows E2E or helper harness that terminates the GUI process and verifies that the Backend PID also terminates at the OS level.
3. Record behavior for Job Object constraints/assignment failures with evidence. Do not claim “GUI-exit containment PASS” before validation.

### Documentation consistency / other review

- §11.3 in `process-backend-isolation-0.9.4.ko/en.md` says the scan does not automatically resume, conflicting with the code and `backend_e2e_test` behavior that replays saved `BackendScanConfig` once. Distinguish lack of exact checkpoint resume from the bounded one-time full rescan after READY.
- The Progress Active Build Queue still carries a 2026-10-07 header and .74-centred rows. Matrix is dated 2026-10-10 and describes .81 as the latest corrective build. Align current focus/next gates with .106 and the October 15 Fast(A) measurement.
- Historical versions such as .74/.75/.76–.82 are labelled “Current” in `BUILD_STATUS.md`, which conflicts with its current .106 header. Mark the older version entries as “Historical.”
- `100.0% · identical content` currently uses size + `quick_hash` (not a full-byte comparison). Include this meaning/limitation in acceptance and separately confirm whether the product requirement demands full byte identity.

### Required OpenCode report format

Report each item as `PASS / FAIL / NOT TESTED / NEEDS DECISION`, with current HEAD, inspected files/functions/tests, commands/results, unresolved questions, and minimal proposed fixes. Keep G4/G6 as “verification required; defect not yet confirmed” until supported by evidence. This interim review does not authorize changing product/engine/DB/schema/cache versions.
